index-100.try: Show monthly revenue by category with an Index toggle that starts every category at 100 in its first month, so small and large categories share one scale.
index-100.mine: Rebase every line to 100 at its first period, so series of very different sizes compare on one scale.
index-100.how: Clicking the Index toggle divides each line by its own first value, so every line starts at 100 on one scale.
index-100.good: Every line starts at 100 in the first period, and switching back shows the original values unchanged.
index-100.goodTry: After clicking Index, every category starts at 100 in Jun 25 on one shared scale, and Parts ends at 84 in Sep 26.

ranking.try: Show a customer leaderboard with each customer's overall rank and rank within their country, and a toggle to keep only each country's leader.
ranking.mine: Show each row's rank overall and within its group side by side, so the leaders stand out.
ranking.how: Each row gets two ranks, one across all rows and one within its group, and a toggle keeps only each group's leader.
ranking.good: The top row overall also ranks first in its group, and the leaders toggle leaves exactly one row per group.
ranking.goodTry: Customer 184 shows #1 both overall and in its country, and Country leaders only keeps one #1 customer per country.

bins.try: Show orders and revenue by order value band, from under $100 to $1,000+, plus a histogram where the reader picks $250 or $500 bins.
bins.mine: Group a number into bands or a histogram, and let the reader pick the bin width.
bins.how: Each value falls into a band or bin, and picking a bin width regroups the values and redraws the histogram.
bins.good: The band counts add up to the total, and a wider bin width shows fewer, taller bars.
bins.goodTry: The bands show 295 orders under $100, 421 at $100-499, 294 at $500-999 and 490 at $1,000+, and $500 bins redraw the histogram.

targets.try: Show 2026 monthly revenue against the monthly target as a dashed line, with attainment % on each bar. Picking a country moves the target with it.
targets.mine: Draw the target as a line that follows the same filters as the actuals, with attainment for each period.
targets.how: The target is drawn as a line that uses the same filters as the actuals, so changing a filter moves both together.
targets.good: Changing a filter moves the target line along with the bars, and periods above the line show attainment over 100%.
targets.goodTry: With all countries the dashed target is $84k. Picking Japan moves it to $8k, and only August beats it, at 160%.

what-if.try: Show revenue by category, actual next to a scenario. The reader sets a price change per category, like Software +10%, and sees the difference.
what-if.mine: Let the reader change an assumption, like a price change, and see the scenario next to the actual result.
what-if.how: Moving a slider changes one assumption, and the scenario recalculates from it next to the unchanged actual.
what-if.good: The scenario and the actual show side by side, and setting every slider back to zero makes them match.
what-if.goodTry: Optimistic (Software +10%, Services +5%) lifts those two scenario bars above actual, and setting every slider to 0% brings the total back to $1,283,053.

cohort-from-rank.try: Rank customers by revenue and let the reader save the top 10% or 25% as a cohort, then compare that cohort with everyone else.
cohort-from-rank.mine: Let the reader pick a rule like top 10%, save the matching rows as a group, and compare it with the rest.
cohort-from-rank.how: Picking a rule like top 10% ranks the rows, saves the matching ones as a group, and compares it with the rest.
cohort-from-rank.good: The saved group's size matches the rule, and the comparison shows the group and everyone else side by side.
cohort-from-rank.goodTry: Picking 10% saves the top 20 customers as Cohort: Top 10% (20), shown side by side with everyone else.

bookmarks.try: Show revenue over time with Country, Date and grain filters. The reader saves the current view as a bookmark and brings it back in one click.
bookmarks.mine: Let the reader save the current filters, sort and grouping as a bookmark and bring that view back in one click.
bookmarks.how: Saving a bookmark records the current filters, sort and grouping, and clicking it later puts them back and reruns the page.
bookmarks.good: After changing several filters, clicking a saved bookmark brings back exactly the view it saved.
bookmarks.goodTry: Saving Japan, Q2 2026, weekly adds a bookmark. After changing the sort, clicking it brings back Japan, Q2 2026 and weekly.

url-state.try: Show revenue over time with Country, Date and grain filters. Share copies the current view as text, and pasting it back opens the same view.
url-state.mine: Let the reader copy the current view as text to send or keep, and paste it back to reopen the same view.
url-state.how: Pressing Share turns the current view into text, and pasting that text back reopens the page with the same settings.
url-state.good: Pasting the copied text after changing filters brings back every filter and setting it held.
url-state.goodTry: Share the view on Japan, Q2 and weekly, change the filters, then paste the text back: the page reopens on Japan, Q2 and weekly.

reset.try: Show revenue with Country and Status filters and a clickable category chart. Each filter chip has an × to clear it, and Reset all clears everything.
reset.mine: Give each active filter a clear button, plus Reset all to return every filter, selection and sort to its default.
reset.how: Each active filter shows as a chip with a clear button, and Reset all returns every filter, selection and sort to default.
reset.good: Clearing one chip leaves the other filters in place, and Reset all shows the same view as a fresh page load.
reset.goodTry: With Japan, Completed and Software selected, the × on one chip clears only that filter, and Reset all returns everything to its default.

undo-redo.try: Show revenue with a Country filter, a grain switch and a clickable category chart. Undo and Redo buttons, and Ctrl+Z, step through the reader's changes.
undo-redo.mine: Let the reader undo and redo their changes to filters and selections, one step at a time.
undo-redo.how: Each change to a filter or selection is kept as a step, and Undo goes back one step while Redo goes forward.
undo-redo.good: Undo removes only the last change, and Redo brings it back, ending on the same view as before.
undo-redo.goodTry: After picking Japan, Week and Software, Undo leaves weekly Japan with no selection, and Redo brings the Software selection back.

saved-views.try: Show revenue with a few filters. The reader saves the current view under a name and reopens it later from a Views list.
saved-views.mine: Let the reader save views under a name and reopen them from a list, for now only during the current visit.
saved-views.how: Saving a view stores its filters under a name, and picking that name from the list later brings the view back.
saved-views.good: A named view appears in the list and, clicked later in the same visit, brings back the settings it saved.
saved-views.goodTry: A view saved as Monday: APAC weekly appears under Views, and clicking it later in the same visit brings back its filters.

refresh.try: Show revenue with a line saying how new the data is, when it was loaded and whether it came from cache, plus a Refresh button.
refresh.mine: Show how new the data is and when it was loaded, with a Refresh button that fetches it again.
refresh.how: A line shows how new the data is and when it loaded, and Refresh skips the cache and fetches everything again.
refresh.good: Pressing Refresh updates the load time, and the freshness line says whether the data came from cache.
refresh.goodTry: The top line shows the newest order date and when the query ran. Run again re-runs nothing, while Refresh re-runs and updates the time.

trend-line.try: Add a dashed trend line to monthly revenue, with Linear, Exponential and Moving average (3 or 6 months) options, a Break down by category toggle, and an option to leave out the incomplete last month.
trend-line.mine: Add a dashed trend line to my time chart, with Linear, Exponential and Moving average options, one line per series when it has a legend, and an option to leave out the incomplete last period.
trend-line.how: The query returns the points; the app fits a straight or exponential line through them, or draws a moving average that the query computes. A month that isn't over yet is left out of the fit.
trend-line.good: The trend follows the filters, each series gets its own line when broken down, and a short last period doesn't drag the line down.
trend-line.goodTry: Across all 16 months the linear trend is −$56 a month. Leaving out September 2026 (23 of 30 days) turns it to +$342 a month. Broken down by category, Software grows +$450 a month and Services falls −$202.
